title: Same octopus, 18 days apart. Left: made with Claude Code alone. Right: Codex concept art + Tripo3D.
author: dept47games

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
The before/after is pretty wild, especially because this isn’t just a prettier static model. You actually carried the Tripo version through rigging and into the creature behavior.

56 bones across the legs sounds like a fun problem 😅

How much cleanup did the Tripo mesh need before you could rig it properly in Godot? I’m curious whether the harder part was getting the geometry ready or actually making eight legs behave naturally.

replies.author: dept47games
replies.body:
Thanks! Funny thing is, my part was mostly the creative-director role. I made the concept image in Codex and turned it into a model in Tripo3D, and after that my job was mostly watching the monitor and saying things like "make it wigglier," "the legs look like a mantis," and "the old one actually looked more like it was swimming."

Claude Code did the actual figuring out. Claude Code was the one who decided to rig the model with a Blender script instead of doing it by hand: find the 8 leg tips, trace each leg, lay 7 bones along it. Claude Code also noticed that where the legs bunch together under the body, skin was getting dragged around by a leg on the other side, and cleaned that up so only neighboring legs share the webbing. The mesh itself barely needed any cleanup, just leveling a 13 degree tilt.

The hard part was the behavior, not the geometry. All the leg motion is code in Godot: waves running down each leg, tips curling and uncurling, a leg reaching out now and then. For the escape swim, we used footage of a real common octopus as the reference. A real one doesn't paddle with its legs. It bundles them behind its body, keeps the body level, skims the bottom, and pulses the bundle open and shut to jet forward. It took several rounds of me going "nope, still not an octopus" before it looked like that.

Honestly it feels like being a manager with a really good employee. I sit back, look at the screen, and complain.😅
